title: Semilinear translated modification product and its invariant isomorphism open
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $H$ be a finite group, with left scheme actions $a_h:X\to X$ and $b_h:S\to S$ satisfying $a_1=b_1=1$, $a_ha_l=a_{hl}$, $b_hb_l=b_{hl}$ and $fa_h=b_hf$. The $b_h$ are induced by a compatible action on $k$, using inverse field automorphisms under $\operatorname{Spec}$. Let $\pi:Y\to X$ be a morphism which is an isomorphism over a dense open $U_0\subset X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and suppose $f\pi$ admits a closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$, with $n\geq0$ [def-kun-projective, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For each $g\in H$ write $Y_g$ for the underlying scheme $Y$ equipped with $q_g=a_g\pi$ and $p_g=fq_g=b_gf\pi$. Put $U=\bigcap_{g\in H}a_g(U_0)$ and form the finite fibre product $P=\prod_{g\in H,X}Y_g$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with $r:P\to X$ and projections $\rho_g:P\to Y$. Then each $p_g$ admits a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$, and $U$ is a dense $H$-invariant open of $X$. There is a left action by scheme automorphisms $A_h:P\to P$ uniquely specified by $\rho_gA_h=\rho_{h^{-1}g}$ for all $g,h$. It satisfies $A_hA_l=A_{hl}$, $A_1=1$, $rA_h=a_hr$ and $frA_h=b_hfr$. The restriction $r^{-1}(U)=P\times_XU\to U$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse defines an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ satisfying $rj:U\to X$ equal to the inclusion and $A_hj=j(a_h|_U)$ for every $h$. Neither action is assumed faithful, and there is no restriction on the characteristic of $k$.

source.place: Tag 01WF, lemma-H-projective-base-change; explicit finite-translate construction in the returned proof of lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification, steps 2, 4 and 5. The averaging route is referenced in de Jong (1997), §2.10, printed p.605 (locally WANTED); the precise action and common-open argument are agent-written.

proof.text: Use the homogeneous-coordinate index set $I=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], so $Q=\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_i:i\in I])$, with projections $t,z$. By [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and [def-pc-fibre-product], $c_g=(b_gt,z):Q\to Q$ exists, since the field automorphism inducing $b_g$ fixes every integer, so $b_g$ commutes with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Its inverse is $(b_{g^{-1}}t,z)$, as both composites have projections $t,z$. Thus $tc_g=b_gt$. The given closed immersion $i$ followed by this isomorphism is still a closed immersion: its image is the homeomorphic image of the closed image of $i$, and its structure-sheaf map is the surjection for $i$ composed with an isomorphism [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Consequently $i_g=c_gi$ is a closed immersion with $ti_g=b_gf\pi=p_g$, into the same projective $n$-space.

proof.text: Each $a_g$ is an isomorphism with inverse $a_{g^{-1}}$, hence a homeomorphism. It sends the dense open $U_0$ to a dense open. A finite intersection of dense opens is dense: intersect any nonempty open successively with these opens; every intermediate intersection stays open and nonempty. This also covers the empty space vacuously. Thus $U$ is dense and open. Moreover $a_h(U)=\bigcap_g a_{hg}(U_0)=U$, since left multiplication by $h$ permutes $H$. An automorphism preserving this open restricts to an isomorphism of the open subscheme, by restriction of its structure-sheaf isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Since $H$ is finite and contains $1$, repeated application of [def-pc-fibre-product] constructs $P$ and gives the following universal property: maps $v:T\to P$ are uniquely determined by maps $v_g:T\to Y$ for which all $q_gv_g$ are one common map $T\to X$. The assertion follows by adjoining one factor at a time using the binary universal property; the one-factor case is $Y_1\to X$. In particular $q_g\rho_g=r$ for all $g$, and maps into $P$ with equal projections are equal.

source.place: Proof (3), direct-image stability route; the finite-translate prerequisite in the inherited ancestry is agent-written, expanding lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification, returned proof steps 2, 4 and 5. The current blueprint paragraph does not state this construction.

proof.text: Fix $h\in H$. The maps $v_g=\rho_{h^{-1}g}:P\to Y$ satisfy $q_gv_g=a_g\pi\rho_{h^{-1}g}=a_ha_{h^{-1}g}\pi\rho_{h^{-1}g}=a_hr$. Apply the universal property of step 3 [def-pc-fibre-product] with common base map $a_hr$ to obtain the unique scheme morphism $A_h:P\to P$ with $\rho_gA_h=\rho_{h^{-1}g}$. This gives $rA_h=a_hr$, and applying $f$ gives $frA_h=fa_hr=b_hfr$.

source.place: Proof (3), direct-image stability route; the finite-translate prerequisite in the inherited ancestry is agent-written, expanding lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification, returned proof steps 2, 4 and 5. The current blueprint paragraph does not state this construction.

proof.text: For every $g$, $\rho_gA_hA_l=\rho_{l^{-1}h^{-1}g}=\rho_{(hl)^{-1}g}=\rho_gA_{hl}$. Projection uniqueness in step 3 [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $A_hA_l=A_{hl}$. Similarly $\rho_gA_1=\rho_g$ gives $A_1=1$. Taking $l=h^{-1}$ in both orders shows that $A_h$ is an automorphism with inverse $A_{h^{-1}}$. Thus these morphisms define the asserted left action.

proof.text: Let $s_0:U_0\to Y$ be the given inverse over $U_0$, so $\pi s_0$ is its inclusion and $s_0\pi$ is the identity on $\pi^{-1}(U_0)$. Write $u:U\hookrightarrow X$. Since $U\subset a_g(U_0)$, the morphism $a_{g^{-1}}u$ factors through the open subscheme $U_0$ by restricting its structure-sheaf map [def-weil-open-immersion]. Define $s_g=s_0(a_{g^{-1}}u):U\to Y$. Then $q_gs_g=a_ga_{g^{-1}}u=u$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $j:U\to P$ with $\rho_gj=s_g$ and $rj=u$. It also gives a lift $\bar j:U\to P_U=P\times_XU$ with $\operatorname{pr}_U\bar j=1$ and $\operatorname{pr}_P\bar j=j$.

source.place: Proof (3), direct-image stability route; the finite-translate prerequisite in the inherited ancestry is agent-written, expanding lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification, returned proof steps 2, 4 and 5. The current blueprint paragraph does not state this construction.

proof.text: Write $e=\operatorname{pr}_P:P_U\to P$ and $d=\operatorname{pr}_U:P_U\to U$. For each $g$, $\pi\rho_ge=a_{g^{-1}}ud$, which factors through $U_0$. Therefore $\rho_ge$ factors through $\pi^{-1}(U_0)$, and the identity $s_0\pi=1$ there gives $s_gd=\rho_ge$. Projection uniqueness for $P$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $jd=e$. Now $d\bar j=1$ by construction, while $\bar jd$ and $1_{P_U}$ have the same two projections $e,d$, so $\bar jd=1$. Hence $d:P\times_XU\to U$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\bar j$.

source.place: Proof (3), direct-image stability route; the finite-translate prerequisite in the inherited ancestry is agent-written, expanding lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification, returned proof steps 2, 4 and 5. The current blueprint paragraph does not state this construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] to $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $r:P\to X$: $U\times_XP\to P$ is an open immersion. Exchanging the two projections by [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies this map with $e:P_U\to P$, so $e$ is an open immersion. Since $\bar j$ is an isomorphism, $j=e\bar j$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion] (the same open image and an isomorphic restricted structure sheaf). Both $A_hj$ and $j(a_h|_U)$ land in $P_U$, because their composites with $r$ equal $a_hu=u(a_h|_U)$. Under the isomorphism $d$ of step 7 their lifts are both $a_h|_U$; uniqueness of its inverse therefore gives $A_hj=j(a_h|_U)$. All constructions used actual scheme morphisms, and require neither faithful actions nor any characteristic assumption.
